idiom_name: hand-rolled { lo, hi, loClosed, hiClosed } object with contains/overlaps
implementation_notes: JavaScript has no interval value: the built-in ways of producing a range are array and generator tricks (Array.from({length: n}, (_, i) => i)) and Intl.NumberFormat.prototype.formatRange, which only formats a numeric pair for display. The realization is therefore a small frozen object or class holding two endpoints plus per-side inclusivity flags (null for an open end) with contains/overlaps/intersect/union methods, and endpoints normalised to a primitive that compares correctly (epoch milliseconds or ISO-8601 strings, never Date objects). Luxon's Interval is the most complete time-domain library option - a half-open interval of DateTimes with contains, overlaps, engulfs, abutsStart/abutsEnd, union, intersection and difference - but choosing it is a project decision, not a language default.
pitfalls: >= on two Date objects does not compare instants (it falls back to valueOf/coercion inconsistently), so endpoints must be epoch milliseconds or ISO strings before any comparison.
Date parsing is implementation-defined for non-ISO input: new Date('2026-01-01') is UTC midnight while new Date('2026-1-1') is local time, so endpoints shift by a day between engines and time zones.

A null endpoint needs an explicit branch in every method: forgetting one makes contains() throw on an open-ended interval, and JSON round-trips drop undefined but keep null, so the representation must be agreed upon.
Mutating range.lo in place invalidates every consumer that cached the interval; freeze the object or rebuild it, and never use a mutable endpoint object (Date) inside a frozen shell.
